{{Quote|You can't fight what you can't see.|[[Urai Fen]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>}}
The '''cloaking device''' was a mechanism capable of rendering an object invisible to either [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] or the naked [[Eye/Legends|eye]] or both.

==Description==
{{Quote|They can't have disappeared. No ship that small has a cloaking device.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]], regarding the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]|<ref name="Episode 5">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
While [[Sensor jammer/Legends|sensor jammers]] could leave a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] invisible to sensors, cloaking devices generated cloaking fields that completely absorbed all incoming sensor scans while shielding the host ship's emissions and reflected energy, thus rendering the starship invisible to both sensors and the naked eye. A single cloaking device unit towered over the average [[Human/Legends|Human]] with a balloon-shaped computer core standing over a series of cloaking field antennas. Below lay the [[Power cell/Legends|power cells]], which were connected to the cloaking field matrix by a series of wires.

[[File:StealthShip-ChristophsisMoon.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Stealth ship/Legends|stealth ship]] cloaking during the [[Battle of Christophsis/Legends|Battle of Christophsis]].]]

The only sensor capable of sensing a "cloaked" vessel was the expensive and rare [[Crystal gravfield trap]], which tracked the gravitational fluctuations created by a large mass in space. Thus, any cloaked vessel was unable to hide from the CGT. However, such cloaking shields also came at a disadvantage to their users because they drained a large amount of energy from the starship's power plant, and (though dependent on the size of the device) a single unit cost millions of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].

The [[Hibridium/Legends|hibridium]] model cloaking device's worst drawback was perhaps the "double-blind" nature of the cloaking shield, which also blocked the host ship's scanners and communication systems. Crews and passengers on cloaked ships were unable to peer beyond the cloak's shroud. Since visual navigation was impossible, any other form of navigation could only be exercised by preprogramming astrogation routes. The vessel was thus effectively isolated from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Communications, combat operations, and sensor sweeps could only occur when the cloaking field was lowered or disabled. The cloaking device did nothing to impair senses dependent on [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], however, and trained [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] could detect even cloaked ships in battle with ease.

Another drawback common to both was that a cloaked ship could be tracked was by the ship's magnetic signature. This tactic, used mostly by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Trench/Legends|Trench]], allowed [[Tracking torpedo/Legends|tracking torpedoes]] to be fired and follow the ship even if it was cloaked.

==Operational history==
{{Quote|Cloaking devices have never been common, but today they are practically non-existent.|Imperial Grand Admiral Martio Batch|<ref name="Handbook" />}}
The [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] planned to utilize [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] to create an invisible stealth armada.

Cloaking devices were once fairly common, based on [[Stygium/Legends|stygium]] crystals mined on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aeten II/Legends|Aeten II]] in the [[Dreighton Nebula/Legends|Dreighton Nebula]]. However, as the crystal supply dwindled, cloaking devices followed suit, until there were none left at all.

[[File:Scimitar_cloaking.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Maul's ''Scimitar'' engaging its cloaking device]]
Before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], cloaking devices were virtually unknown, but not unheard of. Around [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], [[Sienar Design Systems/Legends|Sienar Design Systems]] developed and built a cloaking field generator for [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul's]] [[Scimitar/Legends|''Scimitar'']], powered by stygium crystals.<ref name="Vehicles">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] also had one, which had been added onto ''[[Slave I|Slave 1]]'' courtesy of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]], by [[22 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. <ref name="Boba Fett: A New Threat">''[[Boba Fett: A New Threat]]''</ref> The [[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]] stated that any ship found with a cloaking device installed should be captured intact if at all possible.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] piloted a [[Stealth ship/Legends|Stealth ship]] with a powerful cloaking device through the [[Christophsis blockade/Legends|Blockade of Christophsis]] commanded by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] Trench. Anakin was able to utilize the stealth ship against Trench by using Trench's own tracking torpedoes against him. Thus the ship helped to break the blockade surrounding Christophsis for the time being.

[[19 BBY/Legends|Later in the Clone Wars]], the fleet of CIS Admiral [[Pors Tonith/Legends|Pors Tonith]] utilized cloaking devices in its ships, including the flagship ''[[Corpulentus]]''. These ships used the device to their advantage during the [[Battle of Praesitlyn]].

The ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', [[Galen Marek]]'s transport, had an experimental cloaking device onboard that used stygium crystals in its operation.

[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Emperor's personal shuttle/Legends|personal]] [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] was also rumored to be equipped with a stygium cloak. By the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Aeten II's reserve of accessible crystals had been depleted, making the manufacture of new stygium-based cloaks a virtual impossibility.

[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]] managed to create a cloak based on [[Hibridium/Legends|hibridium]] obtained from [[Garos IV]], but it was inefficient and suffered from double blindness&mdash;occupants of a starship using one could no more see the rest of the galaxy than the rest of the galaxy could see them. This double blindness limited its military effectiveness.

Batch sent the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']] to Aeten II, where it blew up the planet, exposing thousands of previously unreachable stygium crystals for Batch to use. He recreated the old stygium technology and applied it to the [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter/Legends|Phantom TIE project]], but [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] saboteurs completely destroyed the project, including an [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] equipped with a stygium cloaking device that housed the project, the ''[[Terror]]'', and Batch was forced to flee.

[[File:Cloaked_TIE_Phantom.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter/Legends|TIE Phantom]] activating its cloaking device.]]
Several weeks before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a Rebel task force led by [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] destroyed a cloaking device project to be implemented on an [[Unidentified Executor-class Star Dreadnought|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] at [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]]. [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], piloting a captured [[TIE/hu "Hunter" Multi-Role Starfighter|TIE Hunter]], flew into the vessel's trenches and destroyed the three cloaking relays. The resulting explosion not only destroyed the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]], but also the [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Imperial shipyard]] in which she was housed.

Palpatine also commissioned a second team to work on the [[Vorknkx Project]], aiming to make improvements to the hibridium cloak under the supervision of Grand Admiral [[Demetrius Zaarin|Zaarin]]. After Zaarin attempted to overthrow the Emperor, control of the Vorknkx Project passed to Grand Admiral [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]. The team successfully equipped the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Vorknkx]]'' with a hibridium cloak but were unable to overcome a problem which made the device unstable when entering hyperspace.

Knowing that Zaarin was obsessed with obtaining the best technology, Thrawn allowed him to capture the Vorknkx, which was destroyed when Zaarin attempted to flee into hyperspace while cloaked.

During the chaotic years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the gangster-turned-warlord [[Tyber Zann]] would utilize a fleet of [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] and [[Destroyer/Legends|destroyers]], as well as [[F9-TZ Transport]]s, equipped with some form of cloaking device. He and his [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Urai Fen]] were also equipped with their own [[Stealth field generator/Legends|personal cloaking devices]].

[[File:Vengeancecloak.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A [[Vengeance-class frigate|''Vengeance''-class frigate]] engages its cloaking device in battle.]]

The original hibridium cloak prototype found its way to the Emperor's store-house on [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]], where it remained hidden until the return of Grand Admiral Thrawn. Thrawn used the technology in a number of creative ways, including hiding a shipload of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] and [[Plasma-Jet Mole Miner|mole miners]] as "empty cargo" in the [[Battle of Sluis Van]]; using cloaked asteroids as a unique siege engine at [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]; and carefully lining up ships above and below a [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]] (with the ones beneath the shield cloaked) so fire from the orbiting ships would appear to pass right through the shield. This tactic led to the conquest and occupation of several [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] member worlds including [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]] and [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]] without the heavy damage to lives, industry, and resources sustained during most conventional planetary invasions.

After Thrawn's death, innovation in finding a use for the device focused on the [[Computerized Combat Predictor]]. Ten years later, the Predictor still performed insufficiently to warrant further hope.

The [[Empire Reborn]] used a shuttle that was equipped with a one-way cloaking device. In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaden Korr]] went to [[Yalara]] on a mission of destroying the planet's cloaking device, to prevent the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] from laying hands on it.

However, the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Grodin Tierce]], who had been created with some of Thrawn's own thought processes, found a new use for the cloaking device, hiding three [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] in the outskirts of the [[Both system|Bothawui system]], guiding them in by use of a comet that barely grazed the cloaking field.

The use of cloaking devices was outlawed by the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty]].<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the Bothan Spies for the Rebels have an ability called Stealth. This is a one way cloaking shield. The one way part may be due to game mechanics. The ''[[Knights of the Old Republic]]'' games also featured stealth-generating belts rendering the user invisible.
